comment: Advisories `npm audit --omit=dev` reports that do not reach the shipped app, each with the reason. scripts/audit-check.js fails on any other advisory; __tests__/DependencyAudit.test.js checks the reasons still hold (who depends on the package, and that the app bundle cannot load it).

advisories.why: Build tool only. Metro (the bundler) reads the project's own image assets with it on the developer's machine to record their width and height; no code in the app requires it and it is not in the JS bundle or the APK/IPA. The DoS needs a crafted JXL/HEIF image, and the only images it ever parses are the repository's own. Upgrading needs image-size 2.x, whose API Metro 0.83 does not use (it passes file paths), so the bundler would break.
Same package and reason as GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq: an ICNS parsing loop in a build-time tool that parses only the repository's own assets.

Not in the app. @solana/web3.js's React Native entry (lib/index.native.js) loads only jayson/lib/client/browser, which requires nothing but uuid and jayson's generateRequest; stream-json is required by jayson/lib/utils.js, the JSON-RPC server's stream parser, which that client never loads, so Metro never bundles it. The advisory concerns stream-json's pick/ignore/filter/replace filters on hostile input, which nothing in the app runs.

Node only. The web Firestore SDK uses it as its Node HTTP/2 transport; the app never imports Firestore (it uses the native messaging module), grpc-js needs Node's http2 and cannot run in React Native, and it is not in the JS bundle. The flaw is in a gRPC server's auth context, which the app never runs.
Node only, as above: a gRPC server's error messages; the app runs no gRPC server and never loads the package.

Test and build tool only. Jest's transform matches the repository's own file globs with it on the developer's or CI machine; it is not in the JS bundle or the APK/IPA, and the patterns it expands are the project's own.
Developer tool only. The React Native command line quotes its own build commands with it on the developer's machine; it is not in the JS bundle or the APK/IPA and never sees input from users.
Test tool only. Coverage configuration loading in Jest; not in the JS bundle or the APK/IPA, and its format strings are the tool's own.

Node only. jayson's server and Node streaming parts use it; the app's Solana client resolves jayson's browser client, which never imports stream-json, and the package is not in the JS bundle. The app parses no JSONC.
Node only, as above: the Assembler is never loaded by the app; RPC answers are parsed by the app's own strict JSON parser.

Developer tool only: the React Native command-line tool and its development server run on the developer's machine and in CI to build and serve the bundle; no code in the app requires it and it is not in the JS bundle or the APK/IPA. The DoS needs a crafted compressed request to the development server, which listens only while a developer runs it.
